text:
Which DeKalb County school had highest enrollment in 2024-25?
S. C. Rojas
Dekalb High School had the highest enrollment among DeKalb County schools, welcoming 1,995 students during the 2024-25 school year, according to the Illinois State Board of Education.
Of the students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year, 50.4% were boys, and 49.6% were girls.
The largest ethnic group among Dekalb High School students was Hispanic, accounting for 35.5% of the student population.
Among the 38 schools in DeKalb County, Sycamore High School ranked second in enrollment with 1,128 students, while Huntley Middle School ranked third with 853 students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year.
Dekalb High School is a part of DeKalb Community Unit School District 428, which generally encompasses schools within DeKalb County with its main office in DeKalb.
In the previous school year, Dekalb High School had the highest enrollment among DeKalb County schools.
Nationwide, public K-12 education spending has approached roughly $857 billion, with average per-student spending near $17,000, funded primarily through state and local sources. Spending varies widely by state, and Illinois ranks above the national average, with roughly $22,000 spent per student when state, local, and federal funding are combined.
Illinois public school enrollment continues a long-term downward trend. According to statewide reporting and education data analyses, total enrollment fell to about 1.85 million students as of the 2023-24 school year, and major districts such as Chicago Public Schools saw further declines—for example, CPS reported a drop of more than 9,000 students between the 2024-25 and 2025-26 counts.
